Subject: Major errors & latency spike on payment-intent path — urgent

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and token-generation latency around 07:45 PT on the payment-intent route. Throughput for that route is effectively degraded (p50 jumped from 60ms -> 2s and error rate ~8% over the last 15m). This is impacting checkout flows for a small but growing % of customers.

Thanks — Aisha

Subject: RE: Major errors & latency spike on payment-intent path — urgent

Quick triage update — initial findings below. I’ll join the bridge now.

Summary of observed signals:
- Autoscaler: short burst of scale-downs on host pool gpu-pool-w-12 between 07:40–07:47 PT followed by rapid scale-up; correlated with increased cold-start latency on a subset of endpoints.
- Model routing: ~17% of requests hit a newly promoted small-quantized variant (q5_202611) in the last 18m. Promoted via an automated canary AB rollout.
- KV cache: cache miss rate for payment-intent prefix increased from 4% -> 42% at spike time.
- Error type: ~65% of 5xx are backend timeout (504) from the runtime layer.

Immediate mitigation path we can action now:
1) Roll back the q5_202611 canary routing (re-route traffic to stable variant) — avoids potential regressions from quantization artifact.
2) Temporarily relax autoscaler downscale thresholds for gpu-pool-w-12 to prevent oscillation.
3) Warm keyset: proactively pre-warm KV cache for payment-intent prefixes (step in runbook).

I’ll apply steps 1 and 2 now (will capture runbook commands and push the autoscale patch). Attaching runbook snippet (runbook_autoscale_patch_v1.txt).

ETA for initial stabilization: 12–15 minutes post-action. Will provide logs and metrics in the bridge.

— Vivek

Subject: Re: Major errors & latency spike on payment-intent path — urgent

Aisha — quick update from the leadership bridge: we’ve identified two correlated causes (a canary routing promotion of a quantized variant and momentary autoscaler oscillation causing cold starts). Immediate actions taken:

- Routing: We revoked the q5_202611 canary and shifted all production traffic to the stable variant (rolled back the routing).
- Autoscale: Relaxed downscale thresholds and pushed a short autoscaler patch to prevent flapping on gpu-pool-w-12.
- Cache: Started proactive KV warm for payment-intent prefixes.

Observed impact so far: error rate dropping from ~8% -> ~2.1% in the first 10 minutes post-action; p50 latency trending down (2s -> 260ms) but still above baseline. We expect most customer flows to see meaningful recovery within 20–30 minutes.

Next update: I’ll share a stabilization note in 30 minutes and an executive summary for your leadership by 11:30 PT. If you can share any spike-specific traces or user impact (eg number of failed checkouts), that will help our RCA.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll own this until fully stabilized.

— Priyom
